answer.summary: when-should-an-international-crisis-begin: international scope is already approved. A supported development with actual actors/interests/commitments and escalation state can feed the existing declaration route. The acting office governs decisions; other people learn public consequences. One persistent crisis, not a new event every weekly sweep. No arbitrary40-year quota; missing behavioral/rate content is distinct from wiring an existing usable origin.

question: The game can put an international crisis in front of a player and take their decision, and has no way to raise one. So: (1) over a forty-year life, how many international crises should a player live through, and how many should require a decision from them rather than merely happening; (2) what should determine whether one begins — nothing in the simulated world plausibly causes one, so is this a drawn rate from a real historical base rate, and if so which base; (3) how should the office a player holds change what they see and what they may decide, since a state legislator and a governor are not in the chain at all while a member of Congress is; (4) what should a crisis actually do that a player can observe, given that it may not move an economic figure or a poll number without a defensible source for the size of the move; and (5) should war powers, which the game already models as a certifiable extension with a clock, be reachable at all in a life that is mostly state and local?

title: What should start an international crisis, when the panel for deciding one already works
usableAnswer: A rate and a source for it. A short list of crisis kinds worth representing, with what each demands of whom. A position on what a crisis may change in the world without inventing a number. And an honest answer on scope: if an international crisis has no place in a game whose player is usually a state legislator, saying so is a usable answer and retires a built system rather than half-wiring it.
whyItMatters: Measured 2026-09-22 at main 62368c1e. WHAT EXISTS: declareInternationalCrisis, internationalCrisisState, pendingInternationalDecisions, decideInternationalCrisis and certifyWarPowersExtension, a complete model with decision options, a war-powers clock and a player panel. THE ONE MISSING LINK: declareInternationalCrisis has zero callers outside tests, and so does certifyWarPowersExtension, while decideInternationalCrisis is wired from the player's own CrisisNoticesPanel. The player can decide a crisis and nothing can give them one. THE SMALLEST HONEST CHANGE: one scheduled producer that draws at an authored rate and declares a crisis, which is a few lines against a finished API. WHAT A PLAYER WOULD SEE: a notice on their crisis panel, in a life where that panel has never shown anything.
